chunks: Ali (ibn Muhammad) from his father from an-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "The testimony of children, when they are made to testify while they are young, is valid when they grow up, as long as they do not forget it."
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of children valid in Islamic law when they grow up?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) regarding the testimony of children (*shahadat al-sibyan*), ensuring that early exposure to legal proceedings does not invalidate their future witness status. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the validity of testimony is contingent upon the witness's memory and recall of the event upon reaching maturity, rather than the age at which the testimony was initially given. This ruling is crucial in inheritance and contract disputes where early childhood observation may serve as evidence.
